label: Figure 3
title: The clearance clocks as the official and reported figures state them
caption: The targets and the measured clocks side by side. Trusted Workforce 2.0 sets 40 days for Moderate Risk and 75 for High Risk end to end [54](#cite:54). Industry initial cases ran 197 days for Secret and 243 for Top Secret in FY2026 Q3 on an all-cases average, with adjudication now the longest segment [126](#cite:126); the FY2026 Q1 figures of 156 and 227 days were on the older fastest-90-percent basis and are not comparable [124](#cite:124). DHS contractor cases took 76 days to investigate and 41 more from a favorable determination to onboarding in the same quarter [125](#cite:125). GAO found the earlier DCSA statistics understated timelines from 2020 to 2024 [56](#cite:56).
how_to_read: Read the basis column before comparing rows: an all-cases average and a fastest-90-percent figure measure different things, and the reporting basis changed in FY2026 Q3. The targets are government-wide goals; the industry rows are what cleared-contractor cases actually took. A recruiter planning an offer-to-start interval uses the longest plausible row for the level the contract requires, not the target.

explain.text: DCSA moved its industry reporting from the fastest 90 percent of cases to the average of all cases in FY2026 Q3, which raised the published figures without a change in the underlying process [126](#cite:126) [54](#cite:54).
At both levels adjudication now takes longer than the investigation itself: 117 days for Secret and 126 for Top Secret [126](#cite:126).

source: Figures are as published in the FY2026 Q3 progress report [54](#cite:54), the NISPPAC slides of September 2026 [125](#cite:125) and the two ClearanceJobs restatements of the DCSA presentations [124](#cite:124) [126](#cite:126); the DCSA chart labels could not be read cleanly, so the vendor restatements are carried with that caveat in the clearance-timeliness controversy record. No conversion.
